newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Chemical to cut ethylene output by 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Chemical to cut ethylene output by 10 pct.

text.p: Mitsubishi Chemical Corp said on Wednesday it will cut its ethylene output by 10 percent, starting from January, in an effort to put downward pressure on the bullish naphtha market.
It also aims to help raise wholesale prices for its petrochemical products such as polyethylene and styrene monomer by slashing its ethylene production, a company spokesman said.
"We intend to continue the cut in production either until naphtha prices fall enough or until the prices of petrochemical products go high enough to make profits," he said.
As a result of the cut in output, the firm will reduce its naphtha purchases by 10 percent, he said.
Naphtha is used as feedstock for ethylene production.
Mitsubishi Chemical, Japan's largest petrochemical firm with an annual ethylene output capacity of 1.45 million tonnes, uses about five million tonnes of naphtha per year.

Near-term naphtha prices on Asia's benchmark open-specification forward contract shot up by about 33 percent in the second half of 1996 due to tight supplies as well as high global crude prices, leaving petrochemical firms' profit margins razor thin.
Mitsubishi Chemical last week said it will lower production of linear low-density polyethylene (LLDPE) by 25 percent starting in January to raise its wholesale prices.
LLDPE is an ethylene-derived resin used to manufacture such products as garbage bags and coverings for agricultural use.
